personalized_opening: The Holiday Grump has such a fun hook, a runaway bride and a grumpy bookseller with a heart of gold. It is also lovely that you moved from Finland to the Waikato in 2006 and now write romcoms set in New Zealand and beyond.

Kissing My Fake Boyfriend sounds like a great addition to your Sisters and Sweethearts series. With more than thirty romantic comedies written from Hawke's Bay, you have clearly built a loyal readership.

Congratulations on Warp, Rinse, Repeat, the sixth and final Tales of a Former Space Janitor book. Following Triana Moore through pregnancy, malfunctioning baby simulators and a very temperamental smart house sounds like a funny and warm way to close out her story.

Congratulations on Bride of the Savage Alien and the way the Survivor Brides of Tajss series keeps building from Bride of the Scarred Alien. A savage alien warrior fated mates story is exactly the kind of escape your readers keep coming back for.

Congratulations on Vindicated and the momentum of the War Brides of the Vandar series, with four books arriving in quick succession. A fierce heroine, a tortured warlord and arranged marriage tension make for a very bingeable setup.

Congratulations on Vexing Valmir and on wrapping up the Ice Planet Clones series. I loved the idea of a heroine giving the most unlikable gladiator on the planet a honey do list before she accepts the bond.

I came across The Cavalryman: Vengeance Road and was drawn to its setting on the Australian goldfields of 1857, where action, battle and romance collide. It is a vivid corner of history for a thriller, and I would love for more readers to hear how the story came together.

I was moved to learn that your historical novels grew out of researching four convict ancestors in your family tree alongside your mother, Sheila Hunter. The Saddler's Song, set in early colonial Australia, carries that family story forward, and readers would value hearing the background behind it.

I loved reading that Elliot: The First Book follows a 12 year old orphan who receives a book laced with cryptic clues, all set in 1898 Ebenezer and rooted in real Hawkesbury River history. Having your earlier novel Only Two longlisted for the ARA Historical Novel Prize is a lovely mark of the care in your research.

I was intrigued by The Tangled Web, with Viola Oswald disguising herself as a boy to search the streets of Maitland in 1892 for a missing child. It is a wonderful mix of mystery and Australian history that readers would enjoy hearing more about.

book_title: The Black Fire Chronicles: The Guardians: Angus the Ageless
personalized_opening: I came across The Black Fire Chronicles and was drawn to how Angus the Ageless opens in 1591 with an eleven year old gifted a talisman by a man with orange eyes. It is also striking that you grew up in Hobart and chose adventure with the Royal Australian Navy over a career in journalism before turning to writing.

book_title: A Gun Is The Thing With Feathers
personalized_opening: I was interested to learn that A Gun Is The Thing With Feathers began as a serialized story and arrived as a full novel in December 2025. The premise of Emma, a bounty hunter who is forced to hunt her childhood best friend Davis Jake, sounds like it has real heart beneath the dystopian setting.

Congratulations on a busy 2026 that has included You Shouldn't Have Answered, a psychological thriller with classic slasher energy built around a phone call nobody should pick up. Your Haunting of Aberdeen Manor series shows how comfortable you are moving between ghostly dread and suspense.

Your novella Necroflora in the Sequel anthology caught my attention, especially the setup of a mining operation in Northern British Columbia where a miner's fall leaves behind only a mysterious shrine. It is also impressive how your stories fit together inside the larger Macrocosm universe.

book_title: Ghost Stories of the Great Lakes
personalized_opening: Ghost Stories of the Great Lakes sounds like a wonderful follow up to your earlier paranormal collections such as Haunted Hamilton and Creepy Capital. A clockwise journey through all five lakes, from phantom vessels to the Marysburgh Vortex, feels perfectly timed for the October release.

Congratulations on finishing The Fidalian Chronicles with Season of Ruin. A trilogy that took thirteen years to bring to its end, with Prince Isanfier and his war against Icaria at the center, is a real achievement for an independent author.

Congratulations on Un été de courage, the seventh book in your Défenseurs du royaume series. Sustaining a clean young adult fantasy series this long, with adventure and romance for readers aged 13 to 17, says a lot about the loyal readership you have built.

Congratulations on Darkfell winning the Christy Award for First Novel, and on the coming release of Firewing on November 17. A story built around Ranele Firewing and choices that echo three hundred years forward sounds like a compelling next chapter for the Darkfell Saga.

Fourteen books into the Ryan Kaine series is a real milestone, and On the Trail, with Kaine stepping in when a crash leaves a grieving husband facing police suspicion, sounds like a gripping addition. As an Irish born author who has built such a loyal readership around one character, your journey feels well worth sharing.

Congratulations on Witch's Lust, the first book in The Witch series. The story of Lottie Wollowes, a village healer accused of witchcraft, and the house that rose over her burned cottage is a wonderfully dark premise, especially with a priest and a pagan witch at its centre.

Congratulations on Lionhearts being shortlisted for Best Horror Novel at the British Fantasy Awards, especially as a title released through your own Northern Republic Press. Henry Oswald's path from a gas explosion in his hometown to a community group with hatred beneath its good intentions is a striking, timely premise.

The idea of Homer's Odyssey retold as a twenty year exile aboard a generation ship, with Captain Ulysses and a cursed crew of 108, is a striking premise for The Blinding. Launching a whole trilogy across 2026 is also a bold move for an independent author. It is easy to see why readers of The Expanse would be drawn to it.

I saw that The Witch Queen of Camelot arrived this September as a villain origin story, with Igraine fleeing an arranged marriage and being rescued by Morgan le Fay. Giving that Camelot backstory its own novel inside your Chronicles of Talahm world is a fresh take on the legend.

I came across Riddles of the Ancestors and was drawn to how it follows Merlin and his twin sister Ganieda from a magical Foretime to modern London, with Avalon and Tir na nOg along the way. It fits so naturally with your earlier Legends of the Grail and Nimue: Freeing Merlin work.

book_title: Sharpened Blade: The Story of Dinah Clark
personalized_opening: I saw that Sharpened Blade tells the true story of Dinah Clark, who was born an indentured servant, earned her freedom and learned to work as a sawyer. It also caught my eye that you have spent years on Arthurian history with your Dark Age Monarch books, so your range as a storyteller is impressive.

Your cozy fantasy There Be Dragons Here, with Hilda and her granddaughter Frida, caught my attention as a warm, small scale adventure set in the larger world of Aedrea. It is also impressive that you moved from LitRPG with Pangea Online into cozy fantasy and have another Tales of Aedrea book coming in November.

Congratulations on bringing The Grand Game to book ten with The Mad God, due this October. Following a dark fantasy LitRPG series across ten books is a real commitment to your readers, and it stood out to me that you are also building the Annals of the Runeguard alongside it.

I enjoyed learning that The Good Guys follows an ex biker trying to turn over a new leaf on the world of Vuldranni. Reaching book sixteen with One Man's Laughter says a lot about the loyal readership you have built around that series.

book_title: The Curse of Dragon Tail Island
personalized_opening: Your pirate fantasy The Curse of Dragon Tail Island sends Captain Trusty Jack Hawk and his Salty Scoundrels after a magical dagger and a legendary island where dragon's blood can be found. The pitch of Dragonlance meets Pirates of the Caribbean, with a second chance at glory at its center, is a great hook for readers.

You'll Be Sorry follows Amelia Montgomery, who spots the man who broke her heart in a magazine on the eve of her fortieth birthday and decides what she wants most is revenge. A woman who rebuilt her life only to face her past is a hook that stays with a reader.

Setting When They Find Me in Expanse, Colorado, a town of 313, and compressing it into five hours in a blizzard bound cabin is a tight, claustrophobic choice. Annie Wolfe hiding with her daughter Coral makes the stakes feel personal from the first page.

Served Him Right opens with a girls' brunch after a breakup that turns dark when Ana Blacksmith's best friend falls gravely ill. The thread of a secret network that uses ancient methods to obtain justice gives a domestic setup a sharp, unexpected edge.

In It's Not Her, Courtney Gray's quiet family vacation ends with a scream from the lakeside cottage next door and a missing niece who may be a victim or the killer. That question of who in a family you can trust is exactly what makes a lake resort setting so unsettling.

Someone Else's Husband begins on a Mount Kilimanjaro climb where Richard meets artist Frankie Callahan and one person does not come back down. Pitting Gretchen Falk's Park Avenue marriage against Frankie's career making exhibition makes the love triangle feel genuinely dangerous.

I Came Back for You turns on a deathbed confession: the convicted killer admits to four murders but not Melanie's, sending her mother Bree Winter back to upstate New York. A mother forced to reopen the worst chapter of her life gives the story real emotional weight.

book_title: The Lady and a Bank Robber
personalized_opening: The Lady and a Bank Robber puts an English countess with a bank alarm invention in the middle of a Granbury heist gone wrong, and I love that your Lady Inventor series is rooted in 1920s Texas. A suspect list that includes the inventor herself is a fun twist on the classic caper.

Your Spider Heist series, built around Blair Morgan and her crew of thieves, has clearly found a loyal audience, and The Talon Gambit makes it six books. Bringing fifteen years of Army experience, from Ranger private to Special Forces captain, to the heist genre is a distinctive combination.

With more than 30 years as a computer engineer behind you, Prompt Execution reads like it comes from someone who knows exactly how smart homes and smartphones could be turned against us. The hunt for a killer who orchestrates murders through connected devices is a chilling premise, and it follows Proxy War as the second book in your Aegis series.

After 32 years spent protecting the nation's critical infrastructure, you have turned that experience into Sleeper Code, and the idea of a self learning piece of code called Phantom waiting patiently inside the power and water systems is unsettling in the best way. It is a strong debut with a genuinely authentic voice behind it.

Setting a murder mystery in the station city of Nicodemia, with Jude Demarco chasing the truth about the wreck of the Benevolent, is a wonderful blend of noir and science fiction in Nicodemia Station Blues. I also admire that you left a tech career in 2020 to write full time, and it clearly shows in the worldbuilding of your technothrillers and cyberpunk westerns.

I came across Dissonance Volume I: Reality and the way the saga opens with aliens arriving in 2026, then jumps ahead to a world sixteen years changed in 2042. A first volume that has already been adapted for the screen says a lot about how visual this story is.

I noticed First Strike, the opening of your Endless War series, arriving on November 17. The idea of John Cole forging his birthdate to enter an experimental enhancement program on Orion, with the Endless hunting that research, is a strong hook.

I saw that Ground State, book 19 of Expeditionary Force, came out in January and sends Joe Bishop and the Merry Band of Pirates across the galaxy to stop the Outsiders. Keeping Skippy's voice fresh across a series that long is no small feat.

I saw that Spawn World, the twenty sixth Undying Mercenaries book, drops this September, and that Legion Varus is promised easy garrison duty until something clamps onto the Scorpio. Centurion McGill choosing to open the ship to space is a gripping turn.

I came across The Heirs of Humanity and the idea of an Emperor building the largest secret fleet in history, partly as a bulwark against an alien invasion he thinks is inevitable. Captain Jacob Mercer setting out to take that fleet is a great turn.

I saw that Eclipse is the fifth and closing book of The Palladium Wars, picking up in the aftermath of a war between six planets. Writing it as a self published release gives you full control over how the series ends.

Your collection Whispers of the Cryptid caught my attention because it sends ordinary people into encounters with the Jersey Devil, Mothman, Bigfoot and the Flatwoods Monster, with settings like the Pine Barrens and Loch Ness. Writing horror since the age of fourteen and now bringing it to cryptid legends is a story readers will want to hear.

I came across The Sea Witch and loved the idea of Alys Tanner fleeing Puritan New England to captain an all female, sorcery wielding pirate crew. A swashbuckling ocean romantasy that kicks off the Salt & Sorcery series gives readers a lot to be excited about.

I saw that Ruby, book thirteen of your Ghost Mountain Wolf Shifters series, arrived in July. Reaching a thirteenth installment says a lot about the readers you have built, and I also noticed your mermaid standalone Siren Song, which shows real range.

I noticed Fairy Charmed, the third book in your Supernatural Sanctuary series, among your recent releases. Your Siren Series with The Mermaid's Escape, Journey and Return also stood out to me as a fun mermaid reverse harem romance.

I saw that Pearl of Illusions launched this June as the first book in The Mermada Series, with Kanta's descent into power and peril set beneath the sea. Planning seven books of a dark Little Mermaid retelling is a big creative commitment, and I wanted to reach out.

I noticed that your Black Swan Event series opens with an interstellar comet that NASA's SWAN telescope detects and that turns out to be anything but harmless. A story where the sky itself becomes the threat, and a family is caught between the truth and the end of the world, feels made for a visual treatment.

I noticed that Recompense, Book 6 of your Conquer the Dark series, follows survivors in a country thrown back to the Dark Ages after an EMP attack. Carrying a series that deep into its sixth book while keeping readers invested in Ayden, Clara and Mia says a lot about the world you have built.

I noticed that you are the author behind the Z-Burbia series, which dropped zombies into the quiet streets of suburbia, and that Under The Shroud arrived in February 2026. Moving between zombie apocalypse fiction and horror collections shows real range, and readers who love the dark are clearly following you.

Finishing a twelve book series with Anything Ghost is a real milestone, and the final case with a ghostly best friend, a talking cat and a heavily pregnant sleuth sounds like a fun way to bring the story full circle. Your Adelaide based cozy world has clearly built a loyal readership.

book_title: Trixie Travers is Captured in Time
personalized_opening: Launching a second series with Trixie Travers is Captured in Time, described as Golden Girls meets Back to the Future, is a bold and fun step after your four Lilly Pilly Creek Ghost Mysteries. A time travel cozy from a South Australian author is a lovely hook.

book_title: Philly Barker and the French Connection
personalized_opening: Writing from the Sunshine Coast about the Yorkshire village of Chipwell is such a charming contrast, and the French buying trip, bold theft and body in the churchyard in Philly Barker and the French Connection make for a great cosy crime setup. Your foodie and travel inspired voice really comes through.

A witchy cozy series set in a small rural Australian town is a distinctive mix, and Reckoning Down Under taking the Trouble Down Under series to book six with green witch magic and dreamscape adventures shows how much readers have embraced it. Your background in regional Victoria adds real heart to the setting.

book_title: Books & Crooks: Small Town Bookstore Mystery
personalized_opening: Relaunching the Charlotte Dean Mysteries with light rewrites, fresh covers and new titles is a smart way to give a loved series new life, and Books & Crooks sounds like a perfect small town bookstore mystery opener. Your Victorian country setting makes the series feel warm and genuine.

book_title: The Mysterious Affair at Styled Magazine
personalized_opening: A book club that stumbles into real life crimes is such a clever premise for readers who love Agatha Christie style puzzles, and reaching book eight with The Mysterious Affair at Styled Magazine is impressive. Running your own indie publishing business from the Byron Bay hinterland adds an inspiring angle.

I came across Finding Flora and was drawn to its community of women homesteaders on the Alberta prairie, each one starting over and running from her past. It is also good to hear that your next novel, Grasslands, is set for spring 2027.

I was struck by the setting of Like Water for Weary Souls, a Sudbury mining town in the Depression where Finnish immigrant sisters carry family secrets. It is also wonderful to see it earn a 2026 IPPY Silver Award in the Canada East Fiction category.

I was moved by the premise of The Promise She Made, built around the 1940 sinking of the SS City of Benares and the two sisters at its heart. It is a powerful piece of history to bring to readers, and your path from Lincolnshire to Toronto adds an interesting layer to your storytelling.

I was intrigued by The Laundryman, a murder mystery that sends two Mounties into the frozen frontier community of Prince Albert in the winter of 1883. It is a vivid and little told corner of Canadian history to build a story around.

I was drawn to On Isabella Street and its 1967 Toronto setting, where two young women from very different worlds share an apartment building during the counterculture years. Weaving in the peace movement and the closing of psychiatric institutions gives the story real depth.

I came across Lianna and the Hombit and was taken by the premise of a grieving thirteen year old who strikes a bargain with a magical birdlike hombit in the land of Nivram. It is also a lovely way to return to the world of your Lucky Diamond trilogy as a prequel. A story about friendship and healing set in such an imaginative world feels like a great fit for our readers.

I came across your Bluestocking Club series and loved seeing how the books move from a quest to a highlander, a pirate and a highwayman, all with such a playful Regency spirit. Collecting books five to eight into a box set feels like a great gift for readers who have been following the series.

I came across Rescued by the Rakish Lord and was drawn to the pairing of Lord Deveril Blackbourne with Selina Wynter, a lady with all the accomplishments but the fiery spirit of a tavern maid. It sounds like a lively Georgian adventure, and a book that must have been fun to write.

I came across The Undercover Heiress and loved the premise of a Manhattan heiress swapping places with a maid below stairs at the Earl of Hartington's estate. Hidden identities and forced proximity make for such a fun Regency setup, and your RITA win for Waltzing with the Earl says a lot about your storytelling.

I came across Lady Rebellious and was charmed by Bianca Devall retreating to her late father's pig farm in the Berkshire countryside, with the Earl of Crowthorne next door. A Regency romance wrapped around a mystery over her husband's death is a combination readers must enjoy.

book_title: Lit for Him: Snowed in and Falling Hard
personalized_opening: The idea of a snowstorm stranding a sports agent inside Noa's Pittsburgh bookshop, with tea, a spare fuzzy sweater and jelly donuts, is such a warm setup for a Hanukkah romance. Your tagline of romance for every body also stood out to me, and it feels like a fit for the cozy readers who go looking for stories like Lit for Him.

Congratulations on the September 2026 release of Love Felt Like This and its launch event at Eagle Eye Books. A grumpy rock star paired with a joyful children's show creator in a cozy small town is a charming pairing, and it should resonate with readers of your earlier book If It Makes You Happy.

Congratulations on Mine To Hold, the second book in your Heartfire Falls series. A broody Alaska hotshot who has spent years as his best friend Kendall's protector, until one quiet small town night changes everything, is a wonderful friends to lovers setup.

I came across Evening the Score and loved the setup of a team mascot running a revenge scheme on a star player, only for the fake feelings to become real. It is also great to see hockey romance written by someone who plays goalie herself and brings an Indigenous perspective to the genre.

I enjoyed learning about As You Ice It, especially the way a summer fling on Oakley Island turns into a second chance when Naomi discovers Camden plays for the Appies. Her son Liam's new hockey obsession is such a sweet way to bring them back together.

I came across Christmas Bells, the twentieth Cottage on Gooseberry Bay mystery, and loved the idea of a Christmas tree lot at the center of a mystery that has been ten years in the making. Reaching book twenty in a series while keeping the holiday setting fresh is a real achievement.

I noticed Americano Accusations, where Monica Brown's coffee truck in Millpond puts her at the heart of the town's secrets after the grumpy mailman turns up dead. A coffee truck as the vantage point for a whole town of suspects is a charming setup for a cozy.

book_title: Hunt for the Silver Dragon: The Curious Cat Spy Club
personalized_opening: I came across Hunt for the Silver Dragon and loved the premise of the Curious Cat Spy Club chasing a stolen cheetah cub and a mysterious silver dragon painted arrow. A middle grade mystery that mixes animal rescue with real clues feels like a great fit for young detectives.

book_title: The Case of the Midnight Mystery
personalized_opening: I enjoyed learning about The Case of the Midnight Mystery, where Scout and her dog Barnaby track down night noises and bare footprints before Blueberry Creek camp's reputation is ruined. A summer camp whodunit with a loyal dog sidekick is a lovely hook for young readers.

Congratulations on The Secret Bookstore Sleuth Society. A locked room mystery in a book themed inn during an ice storm, with four best friends and an armchair detective Grandma Ida, sounds like such a fun start to a new series.

Congratulations on Endgame. The setup of an ER nurse and a veteran hockey player who cross paths again after one unforgettable night, then try a friends with benefits arrangement, is a great hook, and I like how it leans into grief and starting over.

Congratulations on launching the Swiftmore University series with What You Made Me Do. An elite athlete and an ambitious STEM-focused heroine as enemies to lovers is a fun campus pairing, and I like that the series blends humor with real mental health representation.

Congratulations on My Darling Bride, the first book in The Darlings. A bookstore manager running from her past who steals a Lamborghini, and the owner who answers with a marriage proposal instead of charges, is such a bold and memorable opening to a series.

Congratulations on Dangerously Ours and the close of the Webs We Weave series. Phoebe Graves, an ex grifter building real roots in a wealthy Connecticut town, and her partner in every con, Rocky Tinrock, make for a thrilling final chapter.

Congratulations on The Grumpiest Billionaire. A nonprofit worker on a cross country road trip to talk a billionaire out of giving away his entire fortune is a delightfully fun premise, and the tight quarters banter sounds like classic Pippa Grant.

It is exciting to see Son of Steel arrive this spring as the second half of the Children of Ash duology, following Axel Ashersson and Petra on a sea voyage to Sida. A Norse inspired world of Häxa witches and a hero whose strength carries a curse is a memorable setup, especially from the author behind The Cartographer's War series.

Unraveled sounds wonderfully atmospheric, with Mia Clementine bargaining to break a beast's curse in the shadow of the Wild Hunt in Penumbra. A gothic Beauty and the Beast retelling where the beast turns out to be a fae king is a fresh and romantic take on a classic.

Congratulations on Revenge and Ruin, the start of The Bone Moon Trilogy. Your Seven Sins series, where love is the worst of crimes in the Commonwealth, has already won Gold Moonbeam and Silver IPPY awards, so readers clearly connect with the way you blend romance and high stakes.

Your memoir One Last Hit follows more than a decade of active addiction, from eight rehab programs to a stretch in Mexico among members of the Sinaloa Cartel, and then the long road to the life you lead now as a father of five. Hosting the One Last Hit Podcast to talk with guests about addiction, trauma, and transformation shows how much purpose sits behind the story.

book_title: When Roles Reverse: A Road Map for Caring for Aging Parents
personalized_opening: Your story of caring for your 90-year old mother with Alzheimer's at home while raising a family, and then writing the road map you wished someone had handed you, stood out to me. When Roles Reverse speaks so directly to the sandwich generation, where kids, careers, and parents all need you at once.

book_title: Chasing Ned Hector: Uncovering the Life and Legacy of a Black Revolutionary War Bombardier and Teamster
personalized_opening: Your work as a living history presenter and researcher, bringing Ned Hector back into the story of the American Revolution, is a powerful foundation for this book. The way you challenge the assumption that colonial Black Americans only played manual labor roles is something I think readers will want to hear about in your own words.

The Viscount's Christmas Wish pairs a kind hearted Addie with a suspicious viscount, and I love the snow, mistletoe and touch of Christmas magic in your clean Regency setup. Your enemies to lovers angle sounds like a perfect holiday read.

His Second-Chance Duchess brings a dowager duchess face to face with the poor vicar she once loved, all while a thief troubles the village. I enjoy that The Darling Duchesses give three widows a second shot at happiness.

The Baron's Open Arms, with Beatrice forming her own society to protect young ladies while falling for her brother's closest friend, has a great forbidden spark. I like how your Scoundrels with Secrets series gives each troubled hero a chance at redemption.

book_title: A Match Made On Duchess Square
personalized_opening: A Match Made On Duchess Square gives readers a matchmaker whose toughest client falls for her instead, and that is such a charming twist. The Silver Duchesses series feels like a warm continuation of your Duchess Square world.

When the Heart Seems Broken follows Lady Henrietta from privilege to service as a companion, with a conspiracy and a determined duke in the mix. I admire the sweet, closed door style you bring to both Regency and frontier romance.

Lord Harcourt's Heist pairs Lady Delia with an old fashioned, bewigged poet who has a plan to take down a shared enemy, and that is a delightful caper setup. I also noticed the variety in Rebel Hearts, including the epistolary Dear Lord Wycliffe.

book_title: She Believed and He Moved Mountains
personalized_opening: Your background as a 911 supervisor and Army civilian who deployed worldwide gives She Believed and He Moved Mountains a real life weight that I found memorable. The idea of twenty four true stories showing how small steps of faith invite answered prayer into everyday life feels both personal and encouraging.

I came across The Awakening of the Spirit and was moved by how you describe the car accident as the death of your old life and the start of surrender and renewal. A memoir that moves from childhood hardship and military service to faith, forgiveness and redemption will resonate with many readers.

book_title: Spirits In My Spirituality: Memoir Of A Homestead
personalized_opening: The moment in Spirits In My Spirituality when a Light tells you that you have a job to do and sends you back is a powerful way into a memoir. Your story of caregiving, faith and carrying on through illness and loss on the homestead sounds like one readers will want to hear about in your own words.

book_title: Dying to See the Light: A Scientist's Guide to Reawakening (Without Nearly Dying)
personalized_opening: As a scientist who has lived through several near death experiences, you bring a rare perspective to Dying to See the Light. I especially like the premise in your subtitle, offering a guide to reawakening without nearly dying, which invites readers in with both curiosity and warmth.

book_title: Sacred Ashes: The Flames of Wisdom
personalized_opening: Sacred Ashes: The Flames of Wisdom grew out of real journal entries and the ashes of a suicide note, and that honesty stands out. A blend of memoir and healing guide about identity, inner child work and awakening that unfolds breath by breath gives readers a gentle place to begin.

Mr. Wong to the Rescue brings Annie Fuller Dawson back in 1883 San Francisco, with the beloved Mr. Wong stepping in to help. It is a treat that your Victorian San Francisco series grows out of your own history doctorate, which gives the whole setting such depth.

In Deadly Fashion drops Prudence MacKenzie into a murder in Manhattan's cutthroat dressmaking world just weeks before her wedding, with her gown slashed to ribbons at the scene. Ten books into the Gilded Age Mystery series, that is a wonderfully dramatic hook.

A Bitter Cut marks the fourteenth Lady Darby mystery, which is a remarkable run for a historical series built around an anatomist's widow turned sleuth. Following her across Scotland book after book, with Verity Kent's 1920s adventures alongside, shows a real range across eras.

Piccadilly Reckoning is the thirty third Rannoch Fraser mystery, and following Melanie and Malcolm Fraser as a married pair of spies through Regency England for that many books is a real achievement. Few series keep a couple at the center of the intrigue for so long.

The Snare of Vengeance sends Hasting from a betrayal in Miklagard back through hostile waters to Armorica, and I like that the saga is grounded in your work as a history teacher of the early medieval world. Six books into the series is a real milestone.

Of Flaw and Scorn opens with the 795 AD raid on Rathlin Island, and pairing a Christian captive with a Viking raider makes for a powerful faith and forbidden love story. It is a bold move to step from your time travel trilogy into the Viking Age.

Land of the Wolf closes The Norsemen Saga with Thorgrim Night Wolf trying to get home to Norway while his son Odd fights King Halfdan the Black. Twelve books following one raider is a remarkable run, and finishing it under your own Fore Topsail Press says a lot.

Lord of the Whale Road continues Einar's Saga in your Viking Blood and Blade series, and with Rise of Bloodaxe following on September 30, it looks like a big season for you. Building a series since 2021 alongside a career in financial services is impressive.
Blood Typed, the first Val Jenkins mystery, follows a Halifax Post books columnist who would rather be on the crime beat, and I enjoyed how it pokes fun at the literary world in Nova Scotia.

book_title: Secret in the Mist: An Abi Wunder Mystery
personalized_opening: A former elementary school teacher, Linda Wilson brings a classroom honed ear for young readers to the Abi Wunder series. Secret in the Mist, released on December 30, 2025, follows Abi and her best friend Jess as a ghost girl rises from the marsh mist in Pine Hill and Abi's gift for sensing souls is called on. A ghost mystery built around a child who can see into others' souls is a memorable premise for middle grade readers.

Your memoir The Animals Who Rescue Me caught my attention, especially how it follows your work with groups like Save The Chimps and the International Anti-Poaching Foundation. The way it links wildlife exploitation to human trafficking feels like a story many readers have not heard before.

Your book The Bird Watching Bucket List feels like a perfect invitation for new birders, and it is a lovely extension of your years as a park ranger. Sharing birding adventures as a bucket list is such an inviting way to bring people outdoors.

book_title: Climbing Through: A Courageous Story of Grit, Healing, and Second Chances
personalized_opening: Your memoir Climbing Through follows your recovery after a serious electrical injury and the long road back to rock climbing. Coming from someone who also runs restaurants in Estes Park, that mix of grit, healing and second chances feels like a story many readers will connect with.

book_title: Eventually a Sequoia: Stories of Art, Adventure & the Wisdom of Giants
personalized_opening: Eventually a Sequoia turns your travel journals into a graphic memoir that moves from the Amazon River to the Arctic Refuge, Nepal, Bears Ears and the redwoods. Pairing your own illustrations with stories of adventure and conservation seems like a rare way to bring readers into those places.

book_title: The Way Out: A True Story of Survival in the Heart of the Rockies
personalized_opening: The Way Out tells a true story of survival in the heart of the Colorado Rockies, and your background as a Breckenridge based journalist who covers mountain life clearly shaped how you approached it. A backcountry trip that becomes a fight to get home is the kind of premise that pulls readers in fast.
I came across Salt & Whispers, the fifth Saltmere Chronicles novel, and the way you weave Cornish folklore, psychic bonds and village secrets into a coastal paranormal romance really stood out.

book_title: Featuring the story behind Don't Eat Your Human Boyfriend
personalized_opening: I was charmed by the premise of Don't Eat Your Human Boyfriend, an ethical ghoul, a food court called Broth with a Bite and an 80s mall setting is a wonderfully fresh take on monster romance.

book_title: Wolf Crowned and your author journey
personalized_opening: Finishing a trilogy is a milestone, and Wolf Crowned bringing the Bound to the Shadow King opening arc to a close with its fae and wolf shifter portal fantasy world caught my attention.

I noticed your April 2026 release, The Damaged Forbidden Protector, an enemies to lovers, forced proximity romance. Moving into full time writing in 2025 and building a steady run of small town romances since your debut is an inspiring path.

I noticed that Glitched Play, with its secret identity and headset romance, sounds like a wonderfully fresh addition to The O'Ryan Family Series, and the fake dating charm of your Sarasota Sharks books stayed with me too.
Scouting the Single Dad arriving this September, as part of your Axes & Endzones series, caught my eye, and a single dad hero is such a loved hook in contemporary romance.

Between the Rogue Exorcist books and the Raven Jones series, you have built quite a body of supernatural horror. Searching for Life, the second Raven Jones book following Searching for Death, sounds like a gripping next chapter for readers who have followed the series.

The setting of Ghosts of Chanterlands, a 1940 wartime evacuee discovering a spectral lonely boy and a secret in the attic, is a beautifully classic ghost story premise. Your focus on haunted, Gothic suspense has clearly made you a favourite among ghost story readers.

These Empty Places follows Claire Roth and Lena Hawkins back to Lake Toxaway after the dam broke in 1916, which is such a vivid, little known piece of Appalachian history to build a novel around. Wildflower Haven, with Valerie and her family's garden and nursery center in Cosby that has been in the family since the 1800s, sounds like such a warm and rooted Smoky Mountain setting. Reaching book seven of the Mountain Home series is a real milestone for you and your readers.

book_title: The Blue Moon Cafe & 24-Hour Occult Emporium

book_title: Rain with a Chance of Deer

book_title: Fizz Bits and Lemonade: A Decodable Graphic Novel

book_title: Guided Readers Purple Collection (UFLI Aligned Decodable Readers)

book_title: The Big Book of Things that Go Bump in the Night

book_title: Charismatic Presence: Five Principles for Magnetic Presentations

The Oya Warrior Goddess Lore Book stood out to me for the way it blends Yoruba wisdom about the goddess Oya with superhero worldbuilding from The Sentinel series. A Black heroine at the center of a mythic vigilante story is exactly the kind of idea readers love to follow.

The Last Marshal caught my eye because of its bold premise, with Bass Reeves pulled from 1889 Indian Territory into a political conflict between Earth and the Lunar Republic in 2270. Pairing a real frontier lawman with hard space opera is a hook that readers of Dune and The Expanse will remember.

I came across The Bone Thief, the Syd Walker sequel to Blood Sisters, and was struck by how Syd, a Cherokee archaeologist with the Bureau of Indian Affairs, is pulled into stolen remains at a wealthy kids camp and the disappearance of a young Native woman. It is also meaningful that you write this from your own background as a citizen of the Cherokee Nation.

I came across Isle of Wrath, your April 2026 romantasy set in Lunaris, where everyone trades their memories for asylum. Ada Acevedo bargaining with the goddess of death to save her twin brother is a gripping way to open a series. It is also an interesting turn for an author so well known for contemporary and mafia romance.

I came across The Hope Once Lost, the fifth Baker Oaks book, which arrived in February 2026. A single mom running a bookstore who offers a grieving stranger a cup of coffee and a listening ear is a lovely, warm way to start a love after loss story. It is clear you build small town worlds readers want to return to.

I came across The Cabin In The Storm, your April 2026 romantic suspense about an artist stranded in a remote Alaska cabin with a mysterious stranger. A deadly snowstorm and buried secrets make for a perfectly tense setting. I also enjoyed learning that you are a Hispanic author from South Texas writing angsty love stories.

I came across Sweet Like Brittle, your August 2026 Alpine Ridge romance. A brittle and sweets shop owner torn between her small town identity and a chance to leave, with her best friend Steve rooted in place, is such a tender setup. I also love that you write slow burn romances with strong Latinx leads.

I came across Masks and Mishaps, the finale of your Streams and Schemes trilogy. Wrapping up a spicy romantic comedy series is no small feat, and I saw that The Art of Revenge is already announced as the start of your Curator Trilogy. I also admire that you balance a full time job with writing competent leads who work hard and love harder.

I came across Cookie Science, your September 2026 follow up to Baking Science. Building a cookie book around the why behind each ingredient and technique, with more than 60 recipes, is a smart way to help home bakers get consistent results. I also enjoy the voice you bring to One Sarcastic Baker.

I came across Baking Simplified, your debut cookbook from March 2026. Showing home bakers how to make breads, cakes and cookies without a stand mixer, long proof times or lots of kneading is a welcome promise. It fits the approachable style you have built with Soko's Kitchen.

I came across 108 Asian Cookies, your October 2025 collection of not too sweet treats from a third culture kitchen. Cookies flavored with ube, miso, tahini and gochujang, shaped with recipes from the Subtle Asian Baking community, feel both personal and communal. Congratulations are in order for the 2026 Gourmand Award as well.

book_title: Oh, Scraps! Small Pieces, Big Designs
personalized_opening: I came across Oh, Scraps! Small Pieces, Big Designs and the idea that scraps and low commitment fabrics can spark improvisation and become cohesive quilts with real personality. It is a refreshing way to look at the scrap bin, especially coming from an award winning quilt artist like you.

book_title: Sock Knitting Success: From Fiber to Foot, Learn to Knit Socks with Confidence
personalized_opening: I came across Sock Knitting Success, your Stitching Success guide arriving this October with 11 original sock patterns. A friendly, photo rich walk from fiber to foot sounds like exactly what knitters wanting to move past the first pair are looking for.

book_title: Craft Without Pain: Injury prevention and self-care for knitters and other makers
personalized_opening: I came across Craft Without Pain, your June 2026 guide to injury prevention and self care for knitters and other makers. Bringing your background as an orthopedic physical therapist to stretches, posture and ergonomic tips feels like a very useful gift to the crafting community.

book_title: Cozy Quilts for the Modern Home: 16 Seasonal Projects
personalized_opening: I came across Cozy Quilts for the Modern Home and loved the idea of four projects for each season, from rainbows and blooms in spring to snowflakes and evergreens in winter. It is a lovely way to bring your Abby Maed designs into the rhythm of the year.

book_title: Weaving Wild Baskets: Techniques and Projects Using Foraged Leaves, Grasses, Vines, and Bark
personalized_opening: I came across Weaving Wild Baskets and was struck by how it connects basketry to foraging, with more than 50 plants to harvest and prepare. Teaching it all from your Stone Ridge studio and now sharing it in a Storey book must feel like a real milestone.

I came across Lark and Legion, Book Two of The Ashland Chronicles, and the way it follows Queen Azaleen Frost and Lark Sutter through a divided post war North America. A sapphic romance wrapped in political intrigue and found family is a lovely combination, and your history background clearly shapes the world.

I was drawn to Until I Die, with Sophia Reeves of the Defiance caught between a resistance and an enemy officer turned spy in the ruins of the United States. Enemies who risk everything for justice and each other make for a gripping premise.

I came across No Safe Hands, the first book in your Safe Hands trilogy, and the way Londyn, fourteen years into the end of the world, is forced into an alliance with Junk when raiders attack. The forced proximity and the green flag hero make for a very inviting setup.

I noticed Vasmora, the concluding book of The Eating Woods trilogy, arriving this October as prophecy, love and loss collide one final time. Readers who first found you through dystopian romances like Juniper Unraveling must be eager to see how the story ends.

book_title: A Shade of Chrome and Malice
personalized_opening: I enjoyed learning about A Shade of Chrome and Malice, Book Two of Celestials of Arcadia, where Gray steps up as Elemental queen after Chrome's devolution. The tainted magic of Arcadia and the pressure on her people make for a dark and compelling continuation.

I was glad to come across Hooded, the third book in your Post-Apocalyptic Fairy Tales series, and the way you pair fairy tale structure with resilient heroines and gruff heroes in a ruined world. Your background in British literature makes the retellings all the more interesting.

I came across The Wetworks Miracle and was struck by the premise of humanity harvesting the Root, the only plant found after fleeing a collapsing home world, with a new kind of person who can hear what the all plant whispers. An eco horror novella that turns human mastery over nature on its head is a memorable thing to put in front of readers.

I came across Desert Heist and was drawn to Nate Wilde, a former Green Beret who trades the battlefield for an archaeology dissertation and then heads into the Empty Quarter to find the lost city of Ubar. It is a great hook, and your nearly twenty years in Special Forces clearly shape the story.

I was intrigued by the premise of Signal Fire, where Sasha and Leo are sent to investigate a novelist whose thrillers keep predicting real terrorist attacks. Bringing back two long loved characters for a first joint mission sounds like a great reward for your readers.

I was struck by the setup of Riptide, with Foster Quinn going from a yacht seizure off Key West to a conspiracy that reaches into Congress. Writing it as a retired Navy fighter pilot alongside a former Force Recon Marine must give the action a lot of authenticity.

I saw that Argentia Station hit number one in Military Action Fiction within three days, and that Darkest Before Dawn continues the Tides of War series with George Wallace. Taking readers back to the Atlantic war at sea is a strong follow up.

I came across Oregon Waterfalls, your 2026 addition to a series that now spans ten photography books on Oregon. I especially liked that you invited 45 fellow Oregon photographers to contribute images, which makes the book feel like a community portrait of the state. Few photographers have documented one place so thoroughly from Ashland to the coast.

I came across The Accidental Illustrator and the way it grew out of 14 years of daily drawing. Seeing 615 backers rally behind it on Kickstarter this summer says a lot about the audience you have built. A book that mixes case studies, interviews and a decade of artwork sounds like a generous look behind the scenes.

I came across The Photographer's Field Guide, 2026 and the way you are sharing it chapter by chapter on Substack. After more than 40 years as a commercial photographer, with studios in LA, Chicago and New York, you have a lot of hard won experience to pass along. It is also great to see you mentoring photographers through Visual Media Strategy.

book_title: The Glitch Art of Rob Sheridan
personalized_opening: I came across The Glitch Art of Rob Sheridan, your first art book, and the strong response on Kickstarter. Exploring the aesthetics of digital corruption, after years of visual work with Nine Inch Nails and Pearl Jam, is a fascinating subject for a hardcover debut. Backers clearly wanted to see the unseen works and the thinking behind them.

I came across Abandoned Echoes of Tennessee, your upcoming November 2026 photography book, which already has pre orders open. Your work documenting forgotten buildings across the state, alongside your Route 66 Roadscapes road trip book, gives readers a real sense of travel through overlooked places. It is impressive to see a Nashville photographer build a shelf of 15 books.

I came across Blood Magic and was drawn to the way it weaves Rapunzel and Sleeping Beauty together, with Fleur Fontaine finding her vampire hunting rival Percy Renaud on her doorstep. An enemies to lovers retelling with that kind of opening scene is a great hook for romantasy readers.

book_title: A Kingdom of Curses: The Emergence
personalized_opening: I was intrigued by A Kingdom of Curses: The Emergence, especially Paege Vailenbyrg as a half-Fae, half-Human outsider in the Wolf ruled kingdom of Elyndria. Starting a series with a heroine caught between two worlds and two very different love interests gives readers plenty to follow into book two.

I came across Paws for Connection and loved the idea of The Bookworm by the Bay, a coastal shop known for wonderful stories and rescue cats. Two children talking their single parents into adopting a pair of inseparable kittens is such a warm way to open the Pages and Paws series, and Sunshine Bay sounds like a place readers would happily return to.

I was delighted to read about Brown-Eyed Earl, the third Earls Trip story, with its Ted Lasso meets Bridgerton energy. A scholarly earl who never expected the title and a lady's companion who devises a shocking plan to escape a blackmailer is such a fun setup, and the country house retreat adds even more charm.

Congratulations on your debut, The Place We Begin. I was drawn to Remi, who has a plan for everything except what to do after she kisses her best friend Eli, and to the Vancouver Island setting during the final year of university. Friends to lovers with found family is a combination readers adore.

I enjoyed seeing Game of Thorns in the Village Flower Shop Mysteries, a paranormal cozy that feels just right for readers who also love your Vampire Knitting Club world. Having written well over a hundred novels from Vancouver, you clearly know how to build cozy towns that readers want to revisit.

I was excited to see Too Cold for Comfort coming this November. As a Manitoba author who writes both romantasy and contemporary romance, you have built a lovely range, and a title like this feels perfectly suited to a cold weather release for readers who love to curl up with a warm love story.

Your Knocknashee series has carried Grace Fitzgerald from Ireland all the way to Savannah in Allied Flames, where she must rebuild after Richard is shot down over occupied France in 1943. Following a character across seven books and a wartime love story is the kind of journey readers love to hear about.

In Other People's Marriages, two couples cross paths outside the same therapist's door every Tuesday night, which is such a sharp setup for a family drama. Telling the story from four sides gives readers plenty to debate afterwards.

book_title: The Irish Cottage by the Sea
personalized_opening: The Irish Cottage by the Sea takes readers to Dingle and back to the McBride family you introduced in A Merry Irish Christmas. A cosy Irish coastal setting with family and friendship at its centre is just what many readers want.

Your Belial series has followed Delaney McPhearson from the buried secrets of The Belial Stone all the way to The Belial End, and reaching book 18 of the Rebirth arc is a real milestone. A series that blends archaeological mysteries with nonstop action and spans more than a decade is a rare thing for readers to follow.

Your Philadelphia FBI Corruption Squad series draws on your 26 years as an FBI special agent, and I understand Spoiled Sport is the next story in that world. Writing a female agent on a Public Corruption and Fraud Squad from real experience gives the books a perspective few authors can offer.

Reaching book 14 of the FBI Agent Jade Monroe Live or Die series is a real achievement, and Blood Test arrived this spring. Keeping a federal agent heroine compelling across that many cases says a lot about the readership you have built.

Buried Reign, the fourth book in your Indie Reign FBI Mystery Series with Karen Guyler, came out in July. Running several FBI mystery series at once, from Olympia Smith to Claire Legacy, shows how strongly your readers respond to this world.

Where She Rests brings FBI agent Nikki Hunt back for a twelfth case of missing people and buried secrets. Sustaining a series through twelve books, after Save Her Family earlier this year, is a milestone I would love to see your readers celebrate.

Ransom, your August release, pairs a glamorous Las Vegas setting with a courtroom psychological thriller built around a master manipulator. Readers who know your Special Agent Tess Winnett FBI books will be curious to see where this standalone takes them.

Reaching book 40 of the Dev Haskell Private Investigator series with Winning Hand is a real milestone. I also enjoyed learning that you split your year between Saint Paul and Dublin, which seems to give the series its mix of crime and humor.

Breadknives and Boomsticks, with a half troll baker who cannot tell a croissant from a crossbow, is such a fun twist on the cozy bakery setting. Congratulations on the October release and on the Kickstarter support behind the deluxe hardcover.

The Cozy Fantasy Cookbook sounds like a delight for readers who love the food in their favorite stories, and a Kickstarter launching on October 6 with a beta test kitchen is a lovely way to bring the community in. It is also great to see an award winning fantasy novelist turning that love of cozy worlds into a cookbook.

Reaching a fifteenth volume of Bigfoot Horror Stories is a real achievement for an independent series, and the Pacific Northwest roots behind it make the tales feel grounded. I also love the story of a documentary watched with your grandfather at age eight sparking your fascination with Bigfoot.

book_title: Mike The Werewolf: A Humorous Werewolf Thriller (Howling Mad Monsters, Book 1)
personalized_opening: The idea of a rural Pennsylvania trash collector whose inner wolf, Winston, controls half his body is a wonderfully funny hook for Mike The Werewolf. It is also fun to see you bring the same monster comedy energy you showed in Bill the Vampire and Bigfoot Hunters to a new series.

Your upcoming novel The Ghost Detectives, slated for July 2026, caught my eye, especially coming from the author of the haunted house novels Stillwell and The After House. Your A Haunting on Long Island series has clearly given readers plenty of reasons to keep the lights on.

Hexy Beast pairs an impulsive chaos witch, Effie Sherwood, with a buttoned up werewolf alpha in a fated mates rom com, which sounds like a very fun third Sherwood Witches book. Launching it as a USA Today bestselling author on September 8 must be an exciting moment for the series.

book_title: Got To Get You Into My Midlife (Good To The Last Death, Book 15)
personalized_opening: Got To Get You Into My Midlife is the fifteenth book in your Good To The Last Death series, which is a remarkable run for a humorous paranormal women's fiction series. A story that mixes a wedding, a death and a kidnapping sounds like exactly the kind of chaos your readers love.

I came across Hidden Seeds, the third book in your Dahlia Series, and was struck by how Natalie's story of loss, betrayal and an unlikely friendship is rooted in a small South Carolina town. Seeing it climb Amazon's new Christian fiction releases this spring must have been a wonderful moment.

Congratulations are in order on seventy novels, and I noticed The Baker, with its Denver bakery and family legacy at the center, arrived in April. Moving from mail order brides of the old West to a modern bakery mystery shows real range.

book_title: Featuring the story behind The Falcon
personalized_opening: I saw that The Falcon, with its Argentine falconer and the girl who raises an abandoned chick, closes out your Wings of the West series this December. Twelve books of gritty, mystical frontier romance is a remarkable run to wrap up.

Your June release, Monk's Bride, caught my eye, and so did the number of mail order bride stories you have put out this year alone. That kind of steady output for readers of Texas set western romance is rare.

book_title: Belle Fourche Legacy and your author journey
personalized_opening: I noticed Belle Fourche Legacy arrived in April, and the way you let a place become a character in your historical romances really stood out to me. It is a lovely approach to frontier storytelling.

With more than forty western historical romances behind you, I was glad to see Red, White & Romance arrive in June. Series like Bad Girls of the West and The Burnett Brides clearly have loyal readers.

book_title: Featuring the story behind Her Heart's Allegiance
personalized_opening: I saw that Her Heart's Allegiance is among your latest releases, and your Sister's Mail-Order Bride Company books show how much fun you bring to the genre. Writing well over a hundred books is an impressive body of work.
I saw that Mallory's Secret, from your Brides of Cedar Falls series, is coming October 9. Pairing clean western historical romance with your Texas contemporary series shows a lovely range.

Your memoir From Rejection to Renowned traces a path from a childhood in foster homes to a life of faith, service in the Army, and work as a chaplain. I was struck that you now channel that story into Kay's Carry On, your nonprofit for foster youth. It is a story that clearly speaks to many who have known the system from the inside.

book_title: It's Okay to Talk About Adoption: An Invitation for Change, Awareness, and Belonging
personalized_opening: Your book It's Okay to Talk About Adoption grows out of your own family's path of adopting a sibling pair through foster care. I also admire that you carry the conversation forward through The Forgotten Adoption Option Podcast, which gives voice to adoptees and those who aged out of care.

Your book The Shell Seeker, which looks at 30 shells from the world's oceans and the stories of the creatures that build them, is a lovely way to bring ocean science to everyday readers. Coming from an ocean scientist whose earlier book Life on the Rocks was a finalist for the LA Times Book Prize, it sounds like a book with real range.

Day One Again sounds like a raw and honest memoir about grief, perfectionism and the pressure of performing competence while falling apart inside. I also noticed you are launching it at The Makers Shed in Deepwater on 5 September, which feels like a lovely way to share it with your community.

I came across Hostile City, the second Cal Jackson thriller following Full Sun, and the way it places a murder hunt inside a tense, divided Glasgow ahead of national elections really stood out. Crime fiction that is so rooted in a real city and its current tensions is something readers look for. It is great to see the series continue into 2026.

I was intrigued by The Silent Watching, the second Queen of Grime thriller, and by the choice to put a crime and trauma scene cleaner like Erin Flett at the heart of an Edinburgh story. It is a fresh angle on Scottish crime, and the touch of black humour you bring to the series sounds like a great contrast to the darker material.

book_title: Poison at the Wild Haggis Bookshop
personalized_opening: I love the premise of Poison at the Wild Haggis Bookshop, where Beth's book subscription boxes in Oban end up linked to a suspicious death. A cosy Highland setting paired with a crime that starts with something as lovely as a book parcel is a charming hook, and it is the kind of detail that bookish readers enjoy.

I noticed that The Murder Tree, your fifth DCI Christine Caplan thriller, is due out this November. The idea of three elderly deaths being linked, with the truth of the victims' identities twisting the investigation, is a gripping setup. Readers who followed Where She Lies will surely be eager for the next case.

I was struck by the setup of The Dark Heart, the seventh DS Max Craigie novel, where a bombing in York seems to point one way and DS Craigie uncovers a darker conspiracy and an elusive figure called The Cashier. Your background in real policing must add a lot of authenticity to a series that has built such a loyal following.

book_title: YOU 2.0: Transform Your Life After Divorce
personalized_opening: Your path to writing YOU 2.0 after going through your own long, costly divorce and then becoming a certified divorce coach in Atlanta really stood out to me. The idea that there is a better way to do divorce, and that it can become a chance to redesign your life, is a message many readers need to hear.

book_title: Unhitched: The Essential Divorce Guide for Women
personalized_opening: Unhitched arriving from Gallery Books in January 2026 is a meaningful addition for women facing divorce. Your thirty years of work with women near Boston, and the Beacon Group Fellowship that trains clinicians to lead divorce support groups, give the book real depth.

book_title: Divorce Happens: A Compassionate Guide to Starting Fresh
personalized_opening: Divorce Happens: A Compassionate Guide to Starting Fresh, which you wrote with Jenny and is coming from Sheldon Press at Hachette UK, sounds like a natural next step from everything you have built at Fresh Starts Registry. Running the world's first divorce registry and hosting the Divorce Happens Podcast clearly shaped the warm, practical approach of the book.

Congratulations on QUANT, the first Russell Quant novel in nearly 15 years. I was struck by how the story pairs Quant's visits to his mother's farmhouse as her memory fades with a widow who is certain her husband was murdered. Your Saskatoon launch on October 1 sounds like a great way to welcome readers back to the series.

Congratulations on Operation Betrayed, the sixth book in your Operation series. Your years as the RCMP's first female senior communications strategist in Newfoundland and Labrador give the series a rare insider feel. It is also exciting that the series has been optioned for film and television.

Flaming Murder caught my eye because the theft of Mortiforde Millie, the town's giant Bonfire Night effigy, sets off such a fun mix of village tradition and murder. It is also lovely that the Marquess of Mortiforde series is now three books deep, with the Welsh Borders setting giving each story its own character.

Reaching your tenth novel with Every Sky a Stranger this fall is a real milestone, especially for someone who was among the first wave of indie writers to qualify for SFWA membership. Your long run of science fiction, from the Halcyone Space books onward, makes this a great moment to introduce the new book to readers.
